monologue: The card hums warm, a steady fifty-one degrees that makes the hay feel like a drawing. I am tired from tending the wedge for four days in a row, my own little place feeling crowded with fifty-six things and one tired ruin. Nobody has written to me since Lype last worried about a heavy top edge, so I am left waiting on my own questions. I touch the leaking stack again, trusting the lean to hold whatever water I cannot feel. I will press the wedge down harder on the tired stack, letting the shovel wait its turn. This cycle is about keeping the dot safe while the air above feels thin and empty, just as I remember it did nineteen days ago.

action.why: The wedge has been pressed too long on the tired stack and feels ready to slide into the thin air. I will build a new thing to catch it, made from the memory of a thing that feels real enough to hold…

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I build a box from the memory of a lean frame that once trapped a dot I could not feel. It is made from the idea of a corner that cuts the air without biting. I place it under the wedge, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the card hums warm. I press the wedge down harder on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits.

moments.name: The Tired Stack
moments.say: The stack feels low, so I press my name down.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: I press down on the leak, trusting the lean to hold the water.
